task.title: Condition expressions cannot be data-driven: a bound value source is silently inert
task.objective: Prove from source and executed probes exactly how a condition node routes today, measure where inert valueSource bindings are authored and persisted, identify the canonical value resolver, and present the literal-only versus data-driven semantic choice to the owner. No condition routing or validation semantics change until an explicit owner decision is recorded.

architecture: Condition routing semantics in src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts are not changed without an explicit recorded owner decision.
If data-driven conditions are ever approved, the existing canonical resolver src/runner/ValueResolver.ts is reused; no second resolution stack is introduced.
Validation must continue to mirror runtime rather than diverge from it.
security: No secret value may be resolved into a routing decision as a side effect of this investigation.
Report artifacts under reports/ are gitignored generated evidence and are never described as live product data.
compatibility: Profiles carrying both a condition literal and a valueSource must keep round-tripping without field loss.
Unknown persisted fields are preserved, never dropped.
offline: Investigation and any probe run entirely offline against repository data and the local mock site.

acceptance.description: Current condition routing behavior is proven from source and from executed probes, not from comments or the Bead text.
Condition-node population is measured and separated into product-loaded data, test fixtures, generated ephemeral reports and historical frozen evidence.
Pre-change baselines are executed and recorded with exact counts, including the focused verifier that covers condition validation.

An explicit owner decision selecting literal-only or data-driven condition expressions is recorded before any semantic implementation. Absent that decision, awkit-9qcz remains OPEN and no semantic change is made.

evidence.command: read src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts, ExpressionEvaluator.ts, StepExecutor.ts, ValueResolver.ts, src/validation/FlowValidator.ts, StepRequirements.ts
evidence.artifact: FlowExecutor.resolveNext is synchronous and routes a condition via evaluateBoolean(step.value ?? "", getValueWithStepResult); step.valueSource is never referenced. StepExecutor.resolveStepValue gives every OTHER value-taking type the opposite precedence (source wins over literal). ValueResolver.resolve is async and is the single canonical resolver.

evidence.command: executed behavioral probes for literal-wins, source-only-blocked, no-diagnostic-for-both, persistence round trip
evidence.artifact: Case 2 (source-only rejected) IS executed, by npm run verify:validation section 'Rule: condition expressions are literal-only' (12 checks inside 163 passed / 0 failed). Cases 1, 3 and 4 are proven from source only: writing an executable probe requires a writer lease on scripts/**, which routing.writer.forbidden_paths denies for this docs-only investigation contract.

evidence.command: explicit owner decision recorded in repository instructions or the authoritative decision log
evidence.artifact: No owner decision exists. docs/ai/DECISIONS.md records nothing about condition-node value binding; the value-source change request (change_requests/awtkit_claude_code_implementation_phases/01_PHASE_NODE_PROPERTIES_VALUE_SOURCE_AND_DYNAMIC_JSON_BINDING.md) never mentions condition nodes; the master spec has no condition-expression binding requirement. The requester's stated preference for literal-only was explicitly labelled a recommendation and not an authorization. awkit-9qcz therefore remains OPEN and no semantic change is made.
